exposure: Gastrointestinal colonization of extended-spectrum b-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-PE)
cohort: The study participants were children under the age of 5 years admitted for febrile illness in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania.
finding: A high prevalence of ESBL-PE faecal carriage (56%) was found among the children, and ESBL-PE colonization was a risk factor for ESBL-BSI, with children with BSI having significantly higher carriage.
